title: Release pipeline: tick and verdict: a release moves on as soon as its before-and-after look is in
why: #317 and #318 (2026-11-27) each waited an hour between their before look and staging. Two causes. First, releases_tick's cron line on live reads */24 (the live read of Scheduled tasks, 2026-11-27 05:50 UTC), while Scheduler::JOBS sets it every 10 minutes and the before-and-after check's design counts on that (handoffs/piece3-check.md §3: "releases_tick (every 10 minutes)"; research/launch-plan-jan1-2026-11-26.md, item 2). Second, the site's read of the verdict file (raw.githubusercontent.com) came back empty from :00 until the late re-ask at 60 minutes, though the file was on main from 05:07:26 (run 45942037912); the job logs nothing, so the wait didn't say why. The fix, as the session manager ruled (2026-11-27, its own release, not the Scheduler bundle): (a) releases_tick puts its own line to every 10 minutes once (BeforeAfter::tickLine, through Scheduler::change's '10min' preset); a later Change on Scheduled tasks is a person's and stays. (b) one advance at a time (a lock), and a release's waiting is cleared only once its verdict is decided, so a step that throws leaves it waiting for the next run, never on staging with nothing waiting for it. (c) the verdict is read through GitHub's contents API on main (DocsRepo::now, with the key; raw only when the API is away), and a release whose verdict isn't there 30 minutes after it was asked says so once on its card, naming the file. Backend only: nothing a visitor sees changes. Reviewed: Tier 4 clear (the CEO, 2026-11-27; it's the launch plan's A.2) and Design: approved (words only). A run that arrives while another holds the lock skips: it returns no line, writes nothing and never errors, and the next run takes it. The 30-minute note has no link to the look's run: the run is named only in the verdict file, which is what's missing when the note is written. Also (the CEO's Tier 4 condition on the check's far-timeout fix, 2026-11-27): a verdict's slow pages reached only through a shared file (its far list) are written on the release's card, at most three, in the Design reviewer's words (2026-11-27): "Before-and-after check: /admin/crawler-review.php (as the test Executive, at 390) timed out, then opened when tried again. Staging is slow there; it's reached only through website/js/tv-ask.js. The IT Manager's lane has it.", or, slow before too, "… was slow before this release too, and still didn't open after it. … The slow-pages ticket has it." A block isn't one (its block says it); Site health's notes aren't copied there. Design: approved with that wording. The ping itself, a widened trust named for the record: /api/releases-pull.php has no secret by design (decisions/0159 §5; Jason, 2026-11-15: any call only makes the site look sooner), and since #314 a web call with no staff session is nobody, so every ping was refused ("not taken: Sign in with your staff login first", fromUpload's need('releases.publish')) and every release waited for the job's next run. Releases::asPing() carries releases.publish, and nothing else, for its one fromGit call, dropped in a finally even when it throws: it takes only builds already merged into main, listed by DocsRepo with the token, nothing from the request, at most once a minute; it never schedules, approves, publishes past staging's checks, turns off, rolls back or moves a verdict on (those stay with the 10-minute job and people). Tier 4 review: CEO, 2026-11-27 (a repair of #314's fallout, Prior Ruling Check yes). The #314 re-audit (the CEO, 2026-11-27) found no other web entry point regressed: every webhook and token endpoint reaches none of the guarded checks. One approved piece dropped (the session manager and the CEO, 2026-11-27, option (a)): beforeafter.yml no longer pings the site once a verdict is committed and the ping never moves a verdict on, so a verdict now waits up to one run of the 10-minute job (every 10 minutes once (a) above puts it back from */24). The slow-page wording on the card is unchanged. Design: approved again after option
